audit_findings.title: Open-ended AFFF liabilities may sit outside both owner earnings and the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; for scale, the resolved $750 million settlement equals 4.5% of the $16.572 billion base equity value or $1.23 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Future settlements, defense costs and remediation payments would reduce OE when paid or require a liability deduction in the equity bridge, net of applicable insurance recoveries.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company is presently unable to predict the outcome or ultimate financial exposure beyond the water systems AFFF settlement discussed above, if any, represented by these matters, and there can be no assurance that any such exposure will not be material.
audit_findings.explanation: The unresolved exposure is real: pending individual or mass actions increased from more than 12,400 at September 2025 to more than 16,515 at June 2026, and the company still cannot estimate the loss. That demonstrates an open claim population, but not a measurable valuation error. Because neither gross exposure nor future insurance recovery is estimable, the record cannot establish materiality or a reliable deduction.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $750 million settlement payments and filed insurance recoveries through every OE year, then obtain claim-level reserves, defense-cost forecasts and insurer allocation estimates. Rerun OE and the bridge with probability-weighted net AFFF cash outflows, avoiding amounts already captured in historical OE.

audit_findings.title: The $1.9 billion uncertain-tax liability may be an unpaid claim omitted from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.9 billion recorded liability, equal to 11.5% of base equity value and $3.11 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The liability must either enter forecast OE through cash-tax payments or be deducted once in the equity bridge; omitting it from both overstates common-equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: At September 30, 2025, the Company had recorded a liability of $1.9 billion for its best estimate of the probable loss on certain of its tax positions, the majority of which is included in other noncurrent liabilities in the consolidated statements of financial position.
audit_findings.explanation: The recorded liability and its absence from the stated bridge are demonstrated. Whether the DCF already captures its settlement through cash taxes is unresolved. A one-for-one bridge deduction would reduce base value from $27.12 to about $24.01 per share, so the issue is valuation-material even though it would not reverse the present conclusion that market price greatly exceeds modeled value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $1.927 billion unrecognized-tax-benefit rollforward and $459 million accrued interest to historical and projected cash taxes. Rerun using either an explicit payment schedule in OE or a present-value bridge deduction, but not both.

audit_findings.title: Consolidated cash-flow add-backs may not belong entirely to parent shareholders
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; continuing-operation noncontrolling income was $3 million in FY2025, or 0.3% of anchor OE, but discontinued-operation noncontrolling income was $219 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Using parent-attributable income with 100% of consolidated D&A or favorable working-capital adjustments can overstate OE, while deducting 100% of consolidated capital expenditure or unfavorable working-capital movements can understate it.
audit_findings.evidence: In July 2025, the Company sold its Residential and Light Commercial ("R&LC") HVAC business, including the North America Ducted business and the global Residential joint venture with Hitachi Global Life Solutions, Inc. ("Hitachi"), of which Johnson Controls owned 60 % and Hitachi owned 40 %.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate material noncontrolling ownership in the former R&LC business, but they do not establish how each OE observation was assembled. The FY2025 continuing-operation parent/noncontrolling difference is small, yet that does not quantify the ownership mismatch in historical add-backs or discontinued cash flows. The existence and direction of any net valuation error therefore remain unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a year-by-year parent-attributable reconciliation of income, D&A, capital expenditure, working capital and other OE adjustments. Separate continuing and discontinued operations and rerun the OE series for any non-parent amounts identified.

audit_findings.title: The historical OE series may mix businesses from different perimeters
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; the model's trend OE is $1,190 million versus the capped $1,133.9 million latest-year anchor, a $56.1 million or 4.9% difference
audit_findings.mechanism: A mixed historical perimeter can distort the OE trend, volatility assessment and selected growth scenarios, although the stated MIN(trend, latest) rule currently caps the anchor at FY2025 OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company determined that the R&LC HVAC business, which was previously reported in the Global Products segment prior to the Company's resegmentation, met the criteria to be classified as a discontinued operation as it represented a strategic shift in the Company's operations and resulted in the exit of substantially all of its residential and light commercial HVAC businesses.
audit_findings.explanation: The divestiture and discontinued-operation classification are demonstrated, but the record does not show whether the 2017-2022 OE observations were reconstructed on the post-divestiture perimeter. Because the current anchor is capped at the lower latest-year figure, correcting history cannot directly raise the anchor under the stated method; it could still change the assessment of normalized conversion, volatility and defensible growth.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct 2017-2025 OE on a consistent continuing-business perimeter, excluding R&LC earnings, sale gains and disposal cash flows and treating other divestitures consistently. Then rerun the trend, too-hard assessment and growth scenarios while retaining the stated latest-year anchor cap.

audit_findings.title: Restructuring cash costs continue after the anchor year
audit_findings.magnitude: $236 million of estimated plan charges remained after FY2025; even treating all of it as an undiscounted equity reduction equals $0.39 per share and 1.4% of base equity value; $85 million of FY2026 cash utilization is filed
audit_findings.mechanism: Post-anchor restructuring cash payments reduce forecast OE in 2026-2027 if the corresponding charges were removed from normalized earnings; noncash charges should not be deducted as cash outflows.
audit_findings.evidence: It is expected that one-time restructuring costs, including severance and other employee termination benefits, contract termination costs, and certain other related cash and non-cash charges, of approximately $400 million will be incurred over the course of fiscal 2025, 2026 and 2027.
audit_findings.explanation: Continuation beyond the anchor is demonstrated, but omission from the model is not established without the OE adjustment ledger. The filed scale is insufficient to change the valuation conclusion: the conservative $236 million gross-charge comparison is only 1.4% of base equity value and includes noncash charges. By June 2026, $118 million of post-anchor charges had already been recognized and only approximately $118 million of the original $400 million plan estimate remained.
audit_findings.action: Insert the filed $85 million FY2026 cash utilization and the supportable cash portion of remaining 2026-2027 costs into the explicit forecast years. Exclude noncash impairments and model the associated $500 million annual savings separately.

audit_findings.title: Tax benefits may have been retained after related charges were normalized away
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $80 million of FY2025 tax benefit; if retained in anchor OE and capitalized at the base operating-PV multiple of 15931/1133.9, approximately $1.124 billion, $1.84 per share or 6.8% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back impairment or restructuring charges without reversing their associated tax benefits inflates normalized after-tax OE, which is then grown and capitalized throughout the DCF.
audit_findings.evidence: For fiscal 2025, the effective tax rate for continuing operations was 12 % and was lower than the statutory tax rate primarily due to the favorable impact of impairment and restructuring charges and the benefits of continuing global tax planning initiatives, partially offset by the unfavorable impact of tax audit resolutions.
audit_findings.explanation: The $80 million tax benefit generated by FY2025 restructuring and impairment costs is filed, but the supplied record does not demonstrate whether the valuation retained that benefit after normalizing the related charges. The quantified potential effect exceeds 5% of base equity value, making the possible asymmetry material pending reconciliation.
audit_findings.action: Trace every FY2025 pretax normalization adjustment to its tax effect. Reverse the applicable portion of the $80 million benefit whenever the related charge is added back, establish a sustainable cash-tax rate, and rerun all scenarios from the corrected after-tax anchor.
